title: SHPRR: An Algorithm for Pure Exploration under Constrained Regret
abstract: arXiv:2610.39837v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Best Arm Identification (BAI) conventionally measures the cost of experimentation by the number of samples collected. In many operational settings, however, the cost of exploration relative to a trusted baseline already in place is equally important. We study BAI under both a fixed sampling horizon and a regret budget. Unlike generic resources considered in constrained pure exploration, regret has a distinctive structure: sampling better arms is less costly relative to the baseline. We theoretically show that the regret cost of exploration decreases across the phases of Sequential Halving, a widely used pure-exploration algorithm. This observation yields improved guarantees on the probability of identifying the best arm and motivates a more effective allocation of the regret budget. translated_title: SHPRR：一种在受限遗憾约束下的纯探索算法
translated_abstract: 最佳臂识别传统上通过收集的样本数量来衡量实验成本。然而，在许多实际运营场景中，相对于已部署的可信基线而言的探索成本同样重要。我们在固定采样预算和遗憾预算的双重约束下研究最佳臂识别问题。与受限纯探索中通常考虑的一般性资源不同，遗憾具有独特的结构特性：相对于基线而言，采样表现较好的臂成本更低。我们从理论上证明，在广泛使用的纯探索算法——连续减半的各个阶段中，探索所产生的遗憾成本会逐渐降低。这一观察为识别最佳臂的概率提供了更优的保证，并启发了对遗憾预算更有效的分配方式。我们提出了带比例遗憾配给的连续减半算法（SHPRR），该方法将遗憾预算前置，使得在剩余臂较多时能够进行更多探索……
tldr: 该论文发现探索的遗憾成本在连续减半算法的各阶段中逐步递减，据此提出SHPRR算法，通过前置分配遗憾预算，在固定采样预算与遗憾预算双重约束下显著提升了最佳臂识别的概率保证。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SHPRR, which exploits the theoretically proven decreasing regret cost across the phases of Sequential Halving and front-loads the regret budget to achieve improved best arm identification guarantees under both a fixed sampling horizon and a regret budget.
